as_written_in_papers.quote: She had a heterozygous c.2126A>G (p.Gln709Arg) variant of TNFAIP3.

cases.statement: One affected carrier (patient 3, 33549127) and her asymptomatic carrier father. 37342083 re-reports both from Kadowaki et al., 2021 (= 33549127); the pipeline already merged them.

people.label: Patient 3
people.key_phenotypes: SLE at 24 years (fever, facial erythema, proteinuria, ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm); type 1 diabetes with anti-GAD antibody at 12; epilepsy from 4; athetoid cerebral palsy after neonatal cardiopulmonary arrest

quotes.quote: Patient 3 was a 24-year-old woman.
She had a heterozygous c.2126A>G (p.Gln709Arg) variant of TNFAIP3.
At the age of 24 years, she had a fever, facial erythema, and proteinuria.
She had developed epilepsy at the age of 4 years and type 1 diabetes with positive anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody at the age of 12 years.
She had suffered from athetoid cerebral palsy due to cardiopulmonary arrest of unknown cause on postnatal day 1.
Her father had the same variant but lacked any symptoms.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The authors call the presentation atypical: SLE and type 1 diabetes rather than the Behçet-like features they describe as the major HA20 phenotype. Trio WES was performed, but no statement on other genes is given; cerebral palsy is attributed to neonatal cardiopulmonary arrest.

quotes.quote: In this study, although patients 2 and 3 were clinically suggested to have atypical inflammatory diseases, we interpreted Ile310Thr and Gln709Arg as being of uncertain significance and likely benign, respectively, based on ACMG standards and guidelines; this is because the impairment of A20 function was not observed by in vitro functional assays performed in this study and the genetic trait is incomplete between families with the same variant while the allele frequency of the variant was low.

The major phenotype of HA20 is Behçet’s disease (BD)-like symptoms, including recurrent aphthous stomatitis, genital ulcers, and intestinal symptoms, but clinical features show diversity, including not only BD-like symptoms but also autoinflammatory and/or autoimmune symptoms.
Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed using genomic DNA from the whole blood of patient 3 and her parents.
She had suffered from athetoid cerebral palsy due to cardiopulmonary arrest of unknown cause on postnatal day 1.

segregation.statement: The father carries the variant and has no symptoms (one unaffected carrier). The mother was sequenced (trio WES and Sanger) but her result is not stated explicitly.

functional.statement: Constructs (myc-tagged A20) in CRISPR A20-deficient HEK293 cells: NF-κB reporter activity suppressed like WT (TNF-α, MYD88 L265P and CARD11 F130V stimuli, and in a Tet-on dose system); protein expression similar to WT; IKKβ-mediated Ser381 phosphorylation similar to WT; deubiquitination of TRAF6 K63 chains not different from WT. Controls: WT, Phe127Cys, Lys417Serfs*4 (deubiquitinase defect) and Cys243Tyr. Q709H and Q709del constructs also suppressed reporter activity.

quotes.quote: A20-deficient HEK293 cells were created by the CRISPR/Cas9 system.
However, the TNFAIP3 variants Ile310Thr and Gln709Arg suppressed the elevation of NF-κB reporter gene activity, similarly to the WT and Phe127Cys.

The variant Glu192Lys could not suppress the increase of activity regardless of the A20 expression level, in contrast to the WT, while the variants Ile310Thr and Gln709Arg suppressed it as well as the WT.
The levels of protein expression for myc-tagged TNFAIP3 variants Glu192Lys and Gln709Arg were similar to the WT expression levels, while that of Ile310Thr was mildly decreased but not abolished.
IKKβ-mediated A20 phosphorylation levels of the variants Glu192Lys, Ile310Thr, and Gln709Arg were similar to that of the WT (Fig. 4b).
The variants Glu192Lys, Ile310Thr, Gln709Arg, and Cys243Tyr did not show differences in deubiquitination from the WT (Fig. 5).
The variant Q709R, Q709H and Q709del could suppress the NF-κB reporter gene activity elevated by co-transfection of *CARD11* GoF mutant.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense substitution, p.(Gln709Arg), in ZnF6 (from the batch HGVS and the paper). The paper describes HA20 as caused by TNFAIP3 mutations; its assays test loss of A20 inhibitory function.

quotes.quote: BackgroundA20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is an early-onset autoinflammatory disease caused by mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene, which encodes the protein A20.
These two variants are located in the functional domains of A20, OTU and ZnF6, respectively.

computational_predictions.statement: PolyPhen-2 0.046, SIFT 0.68, CADD 11.04 (third column); the authors summarise the predictions as tolerated; Gln709 lies in a partially conserved region.

The sequence alignment evaluated by Basic Local Alignment Search Tool (BLAST, https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Blast.cgi#) showed that Glu192 is located at a highly conserved region and Ile310 and Gln709 are located at partially conserved regions (Supplementary Table S2).

authors_classification.statement: 33549127 classifies the variant as 'Likely benign' (ACMG) and does not rule out low penetrance; 37342083 repeats 'Likely benign'.

quotes.quote: | Variant classification | Likely pathogenic | Uncertain significance | Likely benign |

In this study, although patients 2 and 3 were clinically suggested to have atypical inflammatory diseases, we interpreted Ile310Thr and Gln709Arg as being of uncertain significance and likely benign, respectively, based on ACMG standards and guidelines; this is because the impairment of A20 function was not observed by in vitro functional assays performed in this study and the genetic trait is incomplete between families with the same variant while the allele frequency of the variant was low.

Although it was difficult to demonstrate the pathological significance by in vitro functional assays, the possibility that TNFAIP3 Ile310Thr and Gln709Arg are low-penetrance mutations could not be completely ruled out, as with the above-mentioned variants.
| Uncertain significance | Uncertain significance | Likely pathogenic | Likely benign | Likely benign |

As for the p.(Gln709Arg) variation, it is considered as likely benign by the authors due to the lack of evolutionary conservation of Gln709 and the absence of protein function alteration (Kadowaki et al., 2021; Table 2).

concerns: 37342083 Table 2 column 13 is a review summary of Kadowaki et al., 2021 (= 33549127); the pipeline already merged both people across papers (HA20-ID0099, HA20-ID0101).
Minor cross-paper difference: 37342083 records 'Recurrent fever: No' for the index case, while 33549127 reports a fever at age 24 (a single episode, not described as recurrent).
The phenotype (SLE, type 1 diabetes, epilepsy, cerebral palsy after neonatal cardiopulmonary arrest) has other possible explanations; the authors describe the presentation as atypical.
Ascertainment: this patient was recruited by personal communication with collaborators, not from the screened series.
All functional data in the batch for this variant point the same way (no loss of function in four assays); the panel should weigh this against the rarity data.
No transcript stated in 33549127; 37342083 uses NM_006290; the batch uses NM_001270508.2 (protein_check: agrees).
notes_for_panel: This candidate is a gap variant in the database sense, but the reporting authors' own assays and assessment point away from a disease role. Included here for completeness.
